questions.prompt: Identical bulbs and identical batteries are used in three circuits. Circuit X: two bulbs in series with a battery. Circuit Y: two bulbs in parallel with a battery. Circuit Z: one bulb with a battery. Which bulbs are brightest?

options.text: Both bulbs in X, because the current passes through two bulbs
options.misconception: More bulbs in the circuit means more light

options.text: Each bulb in Y only, because parallel circuits are always brighter
options.misconception: Parallel is brighter than a single bulb

options.text: The bulb in Z and each bulb in Y, all equally bright
The bulb in Z only, because it is the only bulb
options.misconception: Branches share the battery's energy, so each parallel bulb is dimmer

questions.explanation: Each bulb in Y is connected straight across the battery, so it gets the same voltage and the same current as the single bulb in Z. In X the two bulbs share the battery's voltage, so each is dimmer.

questions.prompt: A battery lights one bulb. A second identical bulb is added in series. What happens to the current in the circuit?

options.text: It stays the same, because the battery has not changed
It gets smaller, because the total resistance is bigger
It gets bigger, because there are more bulbs to push it through
It is used up by the first bulb, so the second bulb gets less
options.misconception: Current is used up (it is energy that is transferred, current is the same all the way round a series loop)

questions.explanation: Two bulbs in series have twice the resistance of one, so with the same battery voltage the current is halved. The current is the same everywhere in the loop, so both bulbs are equally (and dimly) lit.

questions.prompt: Which of these objects would a magnet pick up?

options.misconception: All metals are magnetic (brass is copper and zinc)
Metals that conduct well are magnetic

questions.explanation: Only a few metals are magnetic: iron, steel, nickel and cobalt. Brass, aluminium and copper are metals but are not attracted to a magnet.

questions.prompt: A student wraps wire around an iron nail and connects it to a battery to make an electromagnet. Which ONE change makes the electromagnet stronger?

options.text: Reverse the connections to the battery
options.misconception: Reversing the current makes it stronger (it only swaps the poles)

options.text: Replace the iron nail with a wooden rod
options.misconception: Any rod will do as a core

options.text: Wind more turns of wire around the nail
Use a longer piece of wire to connect the battery to the coil
options.misconception: More wire anywhere means a stronger magnet

questions.explanation: More turns of wire in the coil makes a stronger magnetic field. So does more current (a bigger voltage) or an iron core. Reversing the battery only swaps the north and south poles, and a wooden core removes the iron, so the magnet gets weaker.
